info.title: Deep Link Engine — control plane
info.description: Link, domain, application, tenant and credential management, plus attribution and analytics reporting. Errors are RFC 9457 problem documents whose type member is one of the stable identifiers documented at https://docs.dle.dev/problems/. Writes accept an Idempotency-Key header: the same key with the same body replays the stored response, and the same key with a different body is a conflict.

post.summary: Creates a template.
post.description: A template is a campaign: creating one gives you a campaign identifier that a link can name, and naming it prefills the UTM parameters, the rules and the target defaults the link does not state for itself.

patch.description: Links already created from the template keep the values they were given. A template is a starting point, not a live inheritance.

delete.description:
Links already created from the template keep the values they were given. A template is a
starting point, not a live inheritance: an edit to a campaign that silently rewrote every link
created from it would make a link's stored definition untrustworthy.

get.description: Search matches the slug and the title case-insensitively. The tag filter is a comma separated list and a link must carry every tag in it. Paging is by cursor: pass the next_cursor of the previous page.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive fragment matched against the slug and the title.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Comma separated tags; a link must carry every one of them.

parameters.name: campaignId
parameters.description: Restrict to one campaign or template.

parameters.name: isActive
parameters.description: Restrict to switched-on or switched-off links.

parameters.name: includeArchived
parameters.description: Include links withdrawn by abuse handling (TC-103).

post.summary: Creates a link.
post.description:
The cache invalidation matters even on a create, because the edge caches the absence of a
slug as well as its presence: without it, a link created a second after somebody mistyped its
URL would keep answering 404 for the length of the negative cache window (ADR-005).

post.summary: Streams a batch of link creations.
post.description: The request body is one BulkLinkItem per line and the response is one BulkLinkResult per line, written as each row is processed. A failing row does not fail the batch. At most two batches per tenant run at once and the row count is capped by Dle:Control:BulkMaxRows, which defaults to ten thousand.

get.description:
A link belonging to another tenant is not in the queryable at all, so it arrives here as an
ordinary miss and leaves as 404 — never 403, which would confirm the identifier exists
(TC-166, SHARED-KERNEL §17.7).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The link identifier, as text because identifiers are 64 bit.

patch.description: Only the supplied fields change. A replacement rule set is validated as a whole, never merged, and a changed target is re-checked against the safety policy. Every change appends a revision.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The link identifier, as text because identifiers are 64 bit.

delete.summary: Removes a link created by mistake.

post.summary: Switches a link off without removing it (FR-104).
post.description: The slug stays reserved and the history stays readable. A link withdrawn for abuse is quarantined instead, which is a different operation with a different answer.

get.summary: Reads the revisions of a link, newest first (FR-107).
get.description:
The stored snapshot is returned as it was written rather than re-projected into the current
response shape. A history that silently changes shape when the API does is not a history, and
the question after an incident is what this link was serving at that moment — including the
fields the current version no longer has.

get.summary: Answers what a given client would get, without generating a click.
get.description: Runs the same routing engine the edge runs and returns the decision together with a line per rule saying why it matched or why it lost. Nothing is written: no click event, no attribution. The explanation is available in English and Slovak through Accept-Language.

post.summary: The rule simulator, with the client described in the request body.
Registers a domain (FR-145).
post.description: Each subdomain needs its own association file and its own entitlement; nothing is inherited from the parent domain. A consent mode override may only tighten the tenant setting, never widen it.

patch.description: The host itself cannot be changed: every short URL in circulation names it. Moving to a new host is register-and-retire.

post.summary: Runs every association check against a domain and records the outcome.
post.description:
The response carries the seven-day propagation notice whether the run passed or failed. An
operator who fixes an association file, sees a green tick, tests on a device that still holds
the cached copy and concludes the fix did not work is the failure this notice exists to
prevent (TC-125).

get.summary: Reads the recent verification runs of a domain.
get.description:
History rather than a single status column, because association file problems are usually
intermittent and the useful question is "since when", not "right now" (§C.6, §C.8).

post.summary: Registers an application.
post.description:
An Android registration whose fingerprints do not look like Play App Signing fingerprints is
accepted with a warning rather than refused. It is legitimate — a build installed straight
from a developer machine is signed with the upload certificate — but it is also the single
most common reason app links work in development and silently stop working in production, and
the operator has to be told at the moment they can still act on it (FR-144, TC-123).

patch.description: Neither the platform nor the bundle identifier can be changed: both are part of the identity the association file publishes. Declaring the Play App Signing fingerprints here is what silences the upload-certificate warning.

get.summary: Lists the keys issued for one application.

post.summary: Issues a key for one application.
post.description: The secret appears in this response and nowhere else. The key authenticates only the two SDK ingestion routes and can never write configuration, which is what makes it safe to ship inside an application binary.

delete.description:
The row is kept and switched off rather than deleted, so that the audit entries referring to
it keep referring to something that exists. The authentication lookup requires
`is_active`, so a revoked key stops authenticating immediately.

get.description:
Separate from the identifier route on purpose. Reading one's own tenant is an ordinary,
viewer-level operation; reading somebody else's is instance administration, and conflating
them would mean every viewer credential carried a route that could address another tenant.

get.summary: Lists every tenant on the instance.

parameters.name: includeDeleted
parameters.description: Whether deactivated tenants are listed too.

post.summary: Provisions a tenant (FR-241).
post.description:
The default consent mode is `aggregate_only`, the mode that needs no consent banner. A
fresh tenant therefore never collects more than the legitimate interest basis supports until
somebody deliberately widens it (§E.6.2, FR-248).

patch.description:
A consent mode change is recorded with the old and the new value. Tightening takes effect on
the next resolve; widening does not retroactively make already collected data lawful, and the
audit entry is what lets that distinction be reconstructed later (§E.6.2).

delete.description:
The row stays. A hard delete would cascade through links, keys and the audit trail, and the
audit trail is the one thing that has to outlive the objects it describes; the soft-delete
filter is what stops the tenant appearing anywhere it should not.

get.summary: Lists the tenant's keys, without their secrets.
get.description: The last-used instant is here so that keys nobody uses can be found and retired.

parameters.name: includeRevoked
parameters.description: Whether revoked keys are listed too.

post.summary: Issues a key (FR-242).
post.description:
A caller may not issue a key more powerful than their own. Without that rule an editor could
mint an owner key and hold every capability the role system was meant to withhold, which is
privilege escalation through the credential endpoint rather than through the policies.

delete.description:
The row is kept so that audit entries referring to it keep referring to something that exists;
the soft-delete filter is what stops it authenticating anything again.

get.description:
The points carry clicks, installs and conversions together because that is what the port
returns: the three come out of one pass over the same window, and splitting them into three
requests would triple the work to produce numbers that have to line up anyway.

requests would triple the work to produce numbers that have to line up anyway.

get.summary: One dimension of the window, grouped and ranked.
get.description: The dimension is resolved against a fixed allowlist before any query is built, so an unknown name is a validation error rather than a failed query.

get.summary: Handles the funnel report: clicks to installs to attributed installs to conversions.
get.description: The totals for the window, and the conversion rate they imply.

get.summary:
Handles the attribution quality report — the deterministic, probabilistic and unmatched
split with the mean confidence of the guesses (ADR-008, §0.2).
get.description: How many installs were matched with certainty, how many were guessed and at what mean confidence, and how many were not matched at all. The unmatched share is published rather than hidden: a measurement product that only shows what it caught cannot be checked, and this number is the argument against the commercial measurement partners rather than a footnote (ADR-008, §0.2).

get.summary: A report as a CSV or Parquet download.
get.description: Streams the report rather than buffering it, so a two year breakdown is a download and not an outage (FR-203).

get.summary: A live view of the window over Server-Sent Events.
get.description: Emits a snapshot whenever the totals move and a heartbeat when they do not. The click stream is written by the edge process, so this polls the analytics store rather than forwarding an in-process event; the shape is already a stream of snapshots, so replacing the poll with a subscription later changes nothing a client can see (FR-206).

GDPR article 20 portability and the DORA article 30 exit plan are the same feature, and this is it: newline delimited JSON per table in a ZIP, streamed straight out of the database. Credential material — key hashes, webhook secrets, account hashes — is never included, and the manifest says so explicitly rather than leaving the gap to be discovered (FR-249, §E.6.4).

post.summary: Recovers the click context of a fresh installation.
post.description: Called once on the first launch after an install. Answers with the strategy that produced the match and how much to trust it; an unmatched install is a 200 with matched=false, not an error. Limited to five calls an hour per install_id (§E.9).

post.summary: Records a batch of client events, link opens included.
post.description: Batched, at most 100 events per request. The link_open event is what makes a direct open through a verified Universal or App Link measurable at all: the operating system opens the application without any request reaching the engine, so without this report the most successful campaigns are the most under-counted (§B.6.4, FR-223). A link_open whose URL resolves to one of the caller's links creates a direct_open attribution with confidence 1.00.

post.summary: Issues the six characters an interstitial page shows the user.
post.description: The deterministic iOS path of ADR-008. The edge has just written a click event and exchanges its identifier for a short lived, single use code the user can read off the screen and type into the application (FR-184, §B.6.3). Only the keyed hash of the code is stored; the plaintext exists in this response and nowhere else.

post.summary: Handles a submission.
post.description: The acknowledgement never reveals whether the reported link exists. A form that answered "unknown link" would tell anyone with a list of candidate slugs which ones are live, which is slug enumeration with the rate limit of a public form rather than of the resolve path.

get.summary: Public keys used to verify DLE signatures.
get.description: Lists every key still inside its validity window, so a key published before it starts signing and a key kept after it stopped are both present. Verifiers should select by the kid carried in the signature and refresh on an unknown one.

get.summary: Lists the reports filed against the calling tenant's links.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Restrict to one status, or `null` for all.

get.summary: Lists the instance operator's triage queue across every tenant.
get.description: Oldest first: the reaction target runs from submission, not from triage.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Restrict to one status, or `null` for all.

post.summary: Records a decision on one report.
Withdraws a link from service.
post.description: A quarantined link is not deleted. It keeps answering 410 with an explanation, because quiet deletion destroys the forensic trail a later complaint has to be answered from.

parameters.name: linkId
parameters.description: The link identifier, as text because identifiers are 64 bit.

post.summary: Returns a withdrawn link to service after a successful appeal.

get.description: The shared secret is never returned; it is shown once, at creation.

post.summary: Registers a postback endpoint.
post.description: The destination is resolved and checked against the same target policy a link is checked against, so a webhook cannot be aimed at a private, loopback or cloud metadata address (T-02). The response carries the shared secret exactly once.

delete.description: Deactivation rather than deletion: the delivery history stays, because it is the only answer to a later question about what was and was not sent.

post.summary: Sends one signed test delivery and reports the result.
post.description: A real, fully signed delivery of type webhook.test through the same dispatcher the worker uses. Synchronous, so the integrator learns immediately whether the endpoint answered and what it answered.

get.description: The integrator's debugger: status, attempt count, response code and error for the recent deliveries, optionally with the exact body that was signed and sent.

variant.description: Variant name reported in analytics, for example `"a"` or `"control"`. Unique within a rule.

percent.description: Share of traffic assigned to this variant, 1..100. The sum over one rule must not exceed 100.

AbVariant.description: One arm of a deterministic A/B split (FR-125).

tenant_id.description: Tenant that owns the reported link.

link_id.description: Reported link, as text because link identifiers are 64 bit.

details.description: Free text supplied by the reporter.

has_reporter_contact.description: Whether the reporter left a contact address, which is stored only as a hash.

created_at.description: When the report was received. The reaction target runs from here.

resolved_at.description: When the report was closed, if it has been.

resolution_note.description: What the operator decided and why.

AbuseReportDetailResponse.description: An abuse report as an operator sees it.

id.description: Report identifier the reporter can quote when following up.

AbuseReportResponse.description: Acknowledgement of an abuse report. Deliberately does not confirm the link exists.

prefix.description: Non secret prefix, used to identify the key in listings and logs.

ApiKeyCreatedResponse.description:
Response to key creation. The secret appears here and nowhere else: only an Argon2id hash is
stored, so a lost key is replaced, never recovered (FR-242, K5 in §E.4.1).

last_used_at.description: When the key was last used, for spotting keys that can be retired.

revoked_at.description: Revocation instant, when the key has been revoked.

ApiKeyResponse.description: Representation of an API key, without the secret.

warnings.description:
Warnings that do not block registration but will bite in production, most often the
            Play App Signing fingerprint mismatch.

deterministic.description: Attributed installs whose match is deterministic, confidence exactly 1.00.

unmatched.description: Installs that could not be attributed at all.

average_probabilistic_confidence.description: Mean confidence across the probabilistic matches only.

AttributionQualityResponse.description:
The honest attribution split. This is the number commercial measurement partners systematically
blur, and stating it plainly is the product argument, not a footnote (ADR-008, §0.2).

dimension.description: Dimension that was grouped by, for example `country` or `channel`.

BreakdownResponse.description: A breakdown of one dimension over the queried window.

key.description:
Value of the grouped dimension. Never `null`: rows whose
            dimension is unknown are reported under the literal key `unknown` rather than dropped,
            so the sum of the rows always matches the totals.

clicks.description: Number of clicks in the group.

installs.description: Number of installs attributed to the group.

value.description:
Summed monetary value of conversions in the group, or
            `null` when the group produced no conversion carrying a value.

BreakdownRow.description:
One row of a dimensional breakdown report (FR-202), for example clicks per country or per
campaign. Rows are ordered by long BreakdownRow.Clicks descending and truncated to
int AnalyticsQuery.Limit.

ref.description: Caller supplied correlation key, echoed back in the result line.

BulkLinkItem.description:
One line of a bulk create request. Streamed as NDJSON so a ten thousand row batch never has to
be buffered whole (FR-103).

ref.description: Correlation key from the request line.

id.description: Created link identifier when bool BulkLinkResult.Ok is true.

short_url.description: Short URL when bool BulkLinkResult.Ok is true.

error.description: Problem type from ProblemCodes when the line failed.

BulkLinkResult.description: Result of one line of a bulk create request.

code.description: The code to display, six characters from the homoglyph-free alphabet.

expires_at.description: When the code stops being redeemable, in UTC.

expires_in.description:
Seconds until DateTimeOffset ClaimCodeResponse.ExpiresAt, so the page can count down without a clock
    of its own.

ClaimCodeResponse.description:
A freshly issued claim code. The plaintext code appears here and nowhere else: storage keeps
only its keyed hash (§E.4.1, K3).

attribution.description: Consent to attribution processing. Without it no cross session linking happens.

ts.description: When consent was captured. Retained so the decision stays auditable.

ConsentDto.description: Consent as recorded by the host application or a consent management platform.

details.description: Free text detail from the reporter.

reporter_email.description:
Reporter contact address. Stored only as a hash, so follow up is possible without
            keeping an identifiable address (§E.6.3).

CreateAbuseReportRequest.description: Body of `POST /api/v1/abuse-reports`. Public and rate limited (FR-245).

name.description: Human readable name, so a key can be identified without revealing it.

scopes.description: Optional narrower scopes within the role.

expires_at.description: Expiry instant. Keys without one never expire, which is discouraged.

bundle_id.description: Bundle identifier or package name, for example `sk.customer.app`.

team_id.description: Apple team identifier, for example `ABCDE12345`. Required on iOS.

cert_fingerprints.description:
SHA-256 signing certificate fingerprints. On Android these must come from Play
            Console App signing, not from the local upload keystore (FR-144).

store_id.description: Store identifier, for example `id123456789` or the package name.

store_url.description: Full store URL used as the redirect target.

custom_scheme.description:
Custom URI scheme, used only as a last resort fallback. Never carry secrets over
            it: any application can claim the same scheme (§A.2.3, CVE-2026-26123).

min_app_version.description: Minimum application version that understands the deep link format.

app_clip_bundle_id.description: App Clip bundle identifier, published in the association file (FR-146).

domain_ids.description: Domains this application is associated with.

host.description:
Host to serve links from, for example `link.customer.sk`. Each subdomain needs
            its own association file and its own entitlement; nothing is inherited (§A.2.1).

is_default.description: Make this the default domain for new links in the tenant.

consent_mode_override.description: Consent mode override for this domain. It may only tighten the tenant setting.

default_language.description: Default language for the interstitial page on this domain (NFR-15).

oneOf.description: Default Open Graph metadata used when a link supplies none.

domain_id.description: Domain that will serve the link.

slug.description:
Custom slug. Omit to have one generated (8 base62 characters, ADR-007). A custom
            slug must be distinguishable from the generated shape, so 3 to 7 or 9 or more characters.

title.description: Human readable title shown in the control plane.

target_url.description: Web fallback target used when no application can handle the link.

deeplink_path.description: Path handed to the application, for example `/product/123`.

routing_rules.description: Routing rules. Must contain exactly one default rule and it must be last (TC-105).

oneOf.description: Open Graph metadata for crawler previews. Falls back to the domain default (FR-105).

utm.description: UTM parameters appended to the web target.

tags.description: Free form tags used for filtering and search (FR-109).

starts_at.description: Instant the link starts serving. Before it the link answers as not found.

expired_url.description: Where an expired link redirects instead of answering 404 (TC-104).

is_active.description: Whether the link is active on creation.

slug.description: Short unique identifier used in URLs and logs.

consent_mode.description:
Consent mode: `off`, `aggregate_only` or `full`. Defaults to
            `aggregate_only`, the mode that needs no consent banner (§E.6.2, FR-248).

url.description:
Destination URL. Validated against the same target policy as a link, so a webhook
            cannot be pointed at a cloud metadata endpoint (T-02).

event_types.description: Event types to deliver, for example `attribution.created`.

is_active.description: Whether the subscription is active on creation.

language.description: BCP 47 language tag reported by the device, for example `sk-SK`.

screen.description: Screen size as width by height in physical pixels, for example `1080x2400`.

tz_offset.description: UTC offset in minutes at the time of the call.

DeviceSignalsDto.description:
Device signals offered for probabilistic matching. Deliberately coarse: nothing here is a
stable device identifier, and the server drops the whole object when consent is missing.

is_default.description: Whether this is the tenant default.

is_active.description: Whether the domain currently serves links.

consent_mode_override.description: Consent mode override, when one is set.

DomainResponse.description: Representation of a registered domain and its verification state.

http_status.description: HTTP status the association file answered with, when a request was made.

redirect_count.description: How many redirects were seen. Any value above zero fails the check (TC-124).

propagation_notice.description:
Operator facing reminder that association file changes take up to seven days to
            reach devices on both platforms (§A.2.1, §A.2.2, TC-125).

DomainVerificationResponse.description:
Result of `POST /api/v1/domains/{id}/verify` (FR-143). The warning list matters as much as
the error list: an Android fingerprint taken from the local keystore instead of Play App Signing
verifies fine in a debug build and then fails silently in production (FR-144, TC-123).

accepted.description: How many events were accepted for processing.

rejected.description: How many were rejected, for example for an unknown type or a stale timestamp.

EventBatchAcceptedDto.description: Acknowledgement of an accepted event batch.

platform.description: Client platform, for events that arrive before a resolve has happened.

events.description: The events. At most int EventBatchDto.MaxEventsPerBatch per request.

EventBatchDto.description:
Body of `POST /v1/events`. Batched on purpose: an SDK on a mobile network should spend one
request, not one per event (FR-226).

name.description: Name of a conversion or custom event, for example `purchase`.

url.description: URL that opened the application, for a `link_open` event.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code accompanying decimal? EventDto.Value.

ts.description: When the event happened on the device. Absent means "on arrival".

EventDto.description:
A single SDK event. `link_open` is the important one: when the operating system opens the
application directly through a Universal or App Link, no HTTP request ever reaches the engine,
so without this report the click is invisible and the most successful campaigns are the ones
most under-counted (FR-223, §B.6.4).

clicks.description: Human clicks in the reported interval.

installs.description: First application opens in the reported interval.

attributed.description:
Installs that were matched to a click by any strategy. Always less
            than or equal to Installs.

conversions.description: Conversion events reported by the SDK in the interval.

conversion_rate.description:
Conversions divided by clicks, rounded to four decimal places.
            Zero when there were no clicks; the value is never extrapolated.

FunnelSummary.description: Aggregated click to conversion funnel for one AnalyticsQuery (FR-202).

InterstitialMode.description: Per-rule override for the interstitial page (FR-162, FR-163).

click_id.description: Identifier of the click the code will stand for.

link_id.description: Link the click belongs to, as a string because the value is a 64 bit identifier.

IssueClaimCodeRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/claim-codes`: the interstitial page asking for the six characters it will
show the user (S3, FR-184, §B.6.3).

kid.description: Key identifier, matching the `kid` segment of a signed token.

kty.description: Key type, for example `OKP` for Ed25519 or `oct` for a symmetric key.

alg.description:
Algorithm the key is used with, one of the constants on
            SignatureAlgorithms.

use.description: Intended use. Always `sig` for the keys this engine publishes.

crv.description: Curve name for elliptic curve keys, for example `Ed25519`.

x.description: Base64url encoded public coordinate of an elliptic curve key.

public_key.description:
Base64url encoded raw public key, for post-quantum algorithms that have no JWK
            registration.

not_before.description:
Instant from which the key may be used, in UTC. A key is published before it
            starts signing so that verifiers have time to fetch it.

not_after.description:
Instant after which the key must no longer be accepted, in UTC. A retired key
            stays published until every signature it produced has expired.

JsonWebKey.description:
One public key published at `/.well-known/jwks.json` so that integrators can verify
webhook signatures without holding a shared secret (§B.7.3, §B.7.4).

id.description: Link identifier as a string, because the value is a 64 bit Snowflake.

host.description: Host the link is served from.

short_url.description: The full public URL, ready to paste.

qr_url.description: URL of the QR image for this link (FR-106).

deeplink_path.description: Deep link path handed to the application.

quarantined_at.description: Set when the link is quarantined after an abuse report (TC-103).

version.description: Version counter, incremented on every change (FR-107).

LinkResponse.description: Representation of a link returned by the control plane.

name.description: Template name, unique within the tenant by convention rather than by constraint.

utm.description: UTM parameters copied into links created from this template.

routing_rules.description: Routing rules copied into a link that supplies none of its own.

target_url.description: Default web fallback target for links created from this template.

tags.description: Tags added to every link created from this template (FR-109).

id.description: Template identifier. It is also the campaign identifier a link refers to.

snapshot.description: The stored link document, exactly as it was written.

LinkVersionSummary.description: One historical revision of a link, as stored (FR-107).

match_type.description:
Strategy name, one of the constants on
            `Dle.Domain.Attribution.MatchTypeNames`.

count.description: Number of attribution records produced by that strategy.

average_confidence.description:
Mean confidence of those records, rounded to two decimal
            places. Exactly `1.00` for every deterministic strategy.

MatchTypeSummary.description:
Distribution of attribution strategies over the reported interval — the data behind the
honest dashboard demanded by ADR-008 ("78 % deterministic, 14 % probabilistic with an average
confidence of 0.71, 8 % unmatched").

image_url.description: `og:image`. An absolute URL; relative values are not resolvable by a crawler.

OgMeta.description: Open Graph and Twitter Card metadata rendered on the preview and interstitial pages.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or `null` at the end.

total.description: Total matching items when the store can supply it cheaply.

PagedResponseOfAbuseReportDetailResponse.description: A page of results plus the cursor needed to fetch the next one.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or `null` at the end.

total.description: Total matching items when the store can supply it cheaply.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or `null` at the end.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or `null` at the end.

PagedResponseOfSdkKeyResponse.description: A page of results plus the cursor needed to fetch the next one.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or `null` at the end.

total.description: Total matching items when the store can supply it cheaply.

reason.description:
Why the link is being withdrawn, or why the withdrawal is being lifted. Recorded in the
audit trail and sent to the owning tenant.

QuarantineDecisionRequest.description: Body of a quarantine or release decision.

id.description: Link identifier as a string, because the value is a 64 bit Snowflake.

deeplink_path.description: Path the application should open, for example `/promo/autumn`.

campaign.description: Campaign name carried by the link.

ResolveLinkDto.description: The link an install was attributed to, reduced to what the client needs to navigate.

install_id.description:
Identifier the SDK generated and persisted for this installation. Deduplication and
            replay protection key off it (FR-188, TC-143).

app_version.description: Host application version, for version scoped routing rules (FR-124).

os_version.description: Operating system version reported by the device.

referrer.description: Raw Google Play Install Referrer string. The deterministic Android path (S1, FR-182).

claim_code.description: Code the user typed from the interstitial page. A deterministic iOS path (S3, FR-184).

login_key.description:
Opaque, already hashed account identifier used to reconcile a web session with a
            signed in user. A deterministic path on both platforms (S2, FR-185).

oneOf.description:
Device signals for probabilistic matching. Sent only when the module is enabled and
            attribution consent was given; otherwise the SDK omits the object entirely (TC-145, TC-146).

Recorded consent. Absent or negative consent disables every non-deterministic
            strategy and suppresses storage of the signals (ePrivacy art. 5(3), §E.6.2).

ResolveRequestDto.description:
Body of `POST /v1/resolve`, the call an SDK makes once on the first launch after install
to recover the context of the click that led to it (§B.7.2, UC-04, UC-05).

matched.description: Whether any strategy matched. When false the app continues its normal onboarding.

match_type.description:
Strategy that produced the match: `none`, `install_referrer`, `login`,
            `claim_code`, `probabilistic` or `direct_open`.

confidence.description: Confidence from 0.00 to 1.00. Exactly 1.00 for deterministic strategies.

oneOf.description: The matched link, when there is one.

params.description: Parameters handed to the application, typically the UTM set of the link plus custom data.

expires_in.description: Seconds this result stays valid. Zero means it is final and must not be re-requested.

ResolveResponseDto.description:
Response to `POST /v1/resolve`. Always states how the match was made and how much to trust
it: a probabilistic result is never dressed up as a certainty (FR-186, ADR-008).

RoutingActionKind.description: What a routing rule does once it has matched (§B.5.4).

id.description:
Stable identifier of the rule, unique within the link. It is written to the click stream as
string RoutingDecision.MatchedRuleId, so renaming it breaks historical reports.

oneOf.description:
The match condition. `null` marks the default rule, which matches every client.
A rule set must contain exactly one such rule and it must be the last one; a set without it
cannot be saved (FR-127, TC-105).

then.description: What to do once the rule matches.

RoutingRule.description:
One routing rule (§B.5.4). Rules are data, never code: they are evaluated deterministically,
in order, and the first match wins (FR-127).

action.description: What the rule does. Determines which of the URL properties below are mandatory.

url.description:
Absolute web URL, mandatory for RoutingActionKind.Web. Must use `http` or `https`.
When absent for any other action, the link's own target URL is used as the web fallback.

deeplink_path.description:
In-app path handed to the application, for example `"/product/123"`. It is a path, never a full URL,
and never comes from the incoming request (TC-164).

store_url.description:
Absolute store URL, mandatory for RoutingActionKind.AppOrStore and
RoutingActionKind.StoreOnly. Existing campaign parameters on this URL are preserved.

referrer_template.description:
Android only. Template for the Play Install Referrer string (§A.2.4), for example
`"dl_cid={click_id}&utm_source={utm_source}"`. Supported placeholders are
`{click_id}`, `{utm_source}`, `{utm_medium}`, `{utm_campaign}`,
`{utm_term}`, `{utm_content}` and `{link_id}`.

interstitial.description: Per-rule override of the interstitial page (FR-162, FR-163).

RuleAction.description: The `then` half of a routing rule (§B.5.4) — what happens once the rule has matched.

platform.description:
Platforms the rule applies to, as lowercase enum names:
`"ios"`, `"android"`, `"desktop"`, `"other"`, `"unknown"`.

oneOf.description: Constraint on the operating system version reported by the client (FR-124).
Constraint on the host application version reported by the SDK (FR-124).

country.description: Countries the rule applies to, as ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 codes in upper case, for example `"SK"` (FR-122).

region.description: Sub-national regions the rule applies to, in the notation produced by the GeoIP provider (FR-122).

language.description: Languages the rule applies to, as lowercase primary subtags, for example `"sk"` (FR-123).

channel.description: Client channels the rule applies to, using the canonical names in ChannelNames.

ab.description:
Deterministic A/B split (FR-125). The variants are laid out as consecutive percentage ranges over the
bucket space produced by short ConsistentBucket.Of(string clickId); if the bucket falls beyond the
accumulated total, the rule does not match and evaluation continues with the next rule.

RuleCondition.description: The `when` half of a routing rule (§B.5.4, FR-121…FR-126).

app_id.description: Application the key is bound to.

prefix.description: Non-secret prefix, used to identify the key in listings and logs.

app_id.description: Application the key is bound to.

SdkKeyResponse.description: Representation of an SDK key, without the secret.

user_agent.description: User agent string to classify. Alternative to the explicit fields below.

at.description: Instant to evaluate time windows against. Defaults to now.

click_id.description:
Click identifier used for deterministic A/B bucketing. Defaults to a fixed sample
            value so repeated simulations are reproducible (FR-125).

SimulateRequest.description:
Query for `GET /api/v1/links/{id}/simulate`. Answers "what happens for an iPhone 15 on
iOS 18 in Slovakia, opened from Instagram" without generating a click event (FR-129).

matched_rule_id.description: Identifier of the rule that won.

decision.description: Resulting decision kind, for example `interstitial` or `store`.

url.description: Web URL that would be produced, when the decision leads to one.

deeplink_path.description: Deep link path that would be handed to the application.

store_url.description: Store URL that would be produced, including the referrer parameter on Android.

ab_bucket.description: A/B bucket derived from the click identifier.

consent_mode.description: Effective consent mode applied during evaluation.

trace.description: Per rule explanation in evaluation order, so a marketer can see why rule 2 lost.

SimulateResponse.description: Outcome of a rule simulation, including why each rule did or did not match.

delivered.description: Whether the endpoint accepted the delivery.

response_code.description: HTTP status the endpoint returned, when it answered.

error.description: Short description of the failure, when there was one.

elapsed_ms.description: How long the attempt took, in milliseconds.

payload.description: The exact body that was signed and sent, so the integrator can replay the check.

signing_key_id.description: Key identifier named in the `v2` slot of the signature.

bucket.description: Inclusive start of the bucket in UTC.

clicks.description:
Number of human clicks in the bucket. Crawler traffic is excluded unless
            bool AnalyticsQuery.IncludeBots is set (FR-205).

installs.description: Number of first application opens attributed to the bucket.

conversions.description: Number of conversion events reported by the SDK in the bucket.

TimeSeriesPoint.description:
One bucket of a time series report (FR-202). Buckets are aligned in UTC according to
TimeGrain AnalyticsQuery.Grain and are returned in ascending order.

TimeSeriesResponse.description: A time series plus the totals for the same window.

from.description: Inclusive lower bound of the campaign window.

to.description: Exclusive upper bound of the campaign window.

hours_utc.description: Hours of the day in UTC during which the rule is live, 0..23. An empty or absent array means "any hour".

days_of_week_utc.description: Days of the week in UTC during which the rule is live, 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday. An empty or absent array means "any day".

TimeWindowPredicate.description:
Time constraint on a routing rule (FR-126). Every component is evaluated in UTC so that a
rule behaves identically on every node, regardless of server locale.

status.description:
The status to move the report to: `triaged`, `confirmed`,
    `rejected` or `resolved`.

resolution_note.description:
What was decided and why. Mandatory: this is the statement of reasons the notice is answered
from, and it is what makes the decision auditable months later.

cert_fingerprints.description:
Replacement SHA-256 signing certificate fingerprints. On Android these must be the Play
Console App signing fingerprints, not the local upload keystore (FR-144, TC-123).

play_signing_fingerprints.description:
Fingerprints known to come from Play App Signing. Supplying them here is what silences the
upload-certificate warning, because it states which of the two the operator believes them
to be.

store_id.description: Store identifier, for example `id123456789` or the package name.

store_url.description: Full store URL used as the redirect target.

custom_scheme.description: Custom URI scheme, used only as a last-resort fallback (§A.2.3).

min_app_version.description: Minimum application version that understands the deep link format.

app_clip_bundle_id.description: App Clip bundle identifier published in the association file (FR-146).

domain_ids.description: Replacement set of domains this application is associated with.

UpdateAppRequest.description: Body of `PATCH /api/v1/apps/{id}`. Every member is optional; only the supplied ones change.

is_default.description: Make this the default domain for new links in the tenant.

is_active.description: Switch serving on or off for this domain.

consent_mode_override.description:
Consent mode override: `off`, `aggregate_only` or `full`. It may only tighten
the tenant setting; an empty string clears the override (§E.6.2).

oneOf.description: Replacement default Open Graph metadata for links on this domain (FR-105).

UpdateDomainRequest.description:
Body of `PATCH /api/v1/domains/{id}`. Every member is optional; only the supplied ones
change.

target_url.description: New web fallback target. Re-validated against the safety policy (§E.3).

routing_rules.description: Replacement routing rule set. Validated as a whole, not merged.

change_note.description: Note recorded in the link version history (FR-107).

UpdateLinkRequest.description: Body of `PATCH /api/v1/links/{id}`. Every member is optional; only the supplied ones change.

UpdateTenantRequest.description:
Body of `PATCH /api/v1/tenants/{id}`. Every member is optional; only the supplied ones
change.

detail.description: Human readable explanation of what to fix.

gte.description: Greater than or equal to this version.

lte.description: Lower than or equal to this version.

VersionPredicate.description:
Version constraint on an OS or application version (FR-124).
All bounds that are present must hold at the same time.

secret.description:
The shared secret, base64 encoded, shown exactly once. Feed it to an HMAC-SHA-256 over
`t + "." + body` to verify the `v1` member of `DLE-Signature`.

signing_key_id.description:
Key identifier of the asymmetric slot at the moment of creation, so an integrator knows
which key of `/.well-known/jwks.json` to look for while testing.

WebhookCreatedResponse.description:
Response to `POST /api/v1/webhooks`. The shared secret appears here and nowhere else
(§B.5.2, §E.4.1 K4).

id.description: Delivery identifier, matching the `id` member of the payload envelope.

response_code.description: HTTP status of the last attempt, when the endpoint answered.

last_error.description: Last error, truncated. Never carries request headers.

next_attempt_at.description: When the next attempt is due.

payload.description: The exact body that was or will be sent.

WebhookDeliveryResponse.description: One recorded delivery attempt, as the customer sees it (FR-204).

WebhookResponse.description: Representation of a webhook subscription. The signing secret is never returned.

ApiKey.description: A control-plane API key, presented as a bearer token or in the X-Api-Key header. The key looks like dle_<prefix>_<secret>; only its Argon2id hash is stored, so a lost key is replaced rather than recovered.

SdkKey.description: A key embedded in a customer application. It authenticates the two SDK ingestion routes and nothing else, and must be assumed extractable from the application binary.
SdkKey.name: X-Dle-Sdk-Key
